clue.text: Prince to stop decider

parts.note: to lay off something is to stop doing it

explanation.surface: A royal is told to stop the deciding match of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-breaking extra match settles a contest, so it is the decider.

clue.text: Continue to be wrapped in a dressing

indicators.note: being wrapped in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: 'a' can mean 'per', as in ten pounds a head
to last is to continue or endure

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a wound covered in a bandage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is used in its rate sense, as in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticking plaster is the British name for an adhesive bandage put over a cut.

clue.text: Choir ceased touring area with large church

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the letters of the two words move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A choir has stopped going on tour around a region that has a big cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A district under an archbishop, centred on a cathedral, is the territory of a large church.

clue.text: Unfathomable over old man rather dismissing sexual attraction

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
your old man is your father, pa

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so those letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: 'quite' can mean 'rather', as in quite good
'it' is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled by an old man who has lost his charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing IT from QUITE leaves QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something you cannot see through is hard to understand, so impenetrable or unfathomable.

clue.text: Fine loose fibres

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
lax means slack or loose

explanation.surface: A description of thin, untidy strands of thread.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant's stem fibres are spun into linen, so the word names those fibres.

clue.text: Old book recalled disorderly town

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so these two letters are taken in reverse order

parts.note: rough means unruly or disorderly

explanation.surface: An old book was taken back from a rowdy town's library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns O B round into BO.
explanation.definitionFit: A municipality with its own charter is a town in the British administrative sense.

clue.text: Support for Harry Potter book getting criticism after a space

indicators.note: after places the word for criticism behind the word for a space

parts.note: room means a space
stick is informal for harsh criticism, as in 'take stick'

explanation.surface: A Harry Potter volume is panned after a gap in the series.
explanation.definitionFit: The young wizard flies on a witch's broom, which holds him up in the air.

clue.text: Studies accommodating suitable changes again

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
apt means suitable

explanation.surface: Someone researches fitting revisions to a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt anew is to modify or adjust once more, so it means alters again.

clue.text: Early closure of one study centre

indicators.note: closing early cuts the word short, removing its final letter

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: One college building shuts ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British short form for a university, a place of study.

clue.text: Hard gamblers neglecting lead horses

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: neglecting the lead means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: punters are betters on horses

explanation.surface: Tough betters ignore the favourite among the horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunters are horses bred and trained for riding to hounds.

clue.text: Councillor taken in by accountant in African city

indicators.note: being taken in by someone puts one piece inside another

parts.note: ACA is Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants
Cllr or CR is an abbreviation for councillor

explanation.surface: A local politician is fooled by a bookkeeper in an African capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like 'deceived', but it is a containment.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Ghana is a city in West Africa.

clue.text: Business share generating praise

parts.note: ado is fuss or business
a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: A stake in a company prompts compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship and deep admiration amount to praise.

clue.text: Corporation suppressing most of plan in recession — it's of no interest

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so the belly holds the other letters

parts.note: corporation is jocular slang for a pot belly, a tum

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the letters are written backwards
most of a word drops its last letter

parts.note: an idea is a plan

explanation.surface: A company squashes a scheme during an economic downturn, which bores everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company but is old slang for a belly; 'in recession' writes the shortened plan backwards as EDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom is the quality of something that holds no interest.

clue.text: Behaving like a child, shut up when holding a toy, at first

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the other letters

parts.note: to immure is to wall someone in, shut them up

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter

explanation.surface: A child is sent to their room clutching a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish or babyish behaviour shows a lack of grown-up development.

clue.text: Distasteful burial needs to be arranged

indicators.note: arranging means putting in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A funeral must be organised, an unpleasant chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' belongs to the fodder, not the surface verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwanted or objectionable is distasteful.

clue.text: Pornographic crime the subject of uproar?

parts.note: blue means smutty, as in a blue movie
murder is a crime

explanation.surface: A sordid killing makes a scandalous news story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scream blue murder' means to protest loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom about shouting loudly, these words are what is screamed, so the object of a racket.

clue.text: Man offering no initial support for worker in the field

indicators.note: having no initial means the first letter is dropped

parts.words: support for worker in the field
parts.note: a shepherd, who works in the fields, leans on a crook

explanation.surface: A man won't give a farmhand any backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is one of the pieces, or men, in chess.

clue.text: Extra words about freedom? They're not seriously meant

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: PS, postscript, adds extra words to a letter
latitude is freedom of action

explanation.surface: A postscript on liberty turns out to be empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite remarks are said for form's sake, lacking any real conviction.

clue.text: Surreptitious about taking Catholic into protection? Hardly at all

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer word wraps the rest

parts.note: sly means sneaky or surreptitious

indicators.note: taking one thing into another puts it inside

parts.note: care means protection, as in 'in care'

explanation.surface: A secretive plan to shelter a Catholic barely happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... into' is split: 'taking' just links, 'into' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely or only just: a synonym for hardly at all.

clue.text: It foresees company taking control of Channel Islands

indicators.note: taking control of means taking hold of, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: presence means company, as in in the presence of
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, Jersey and Guernsey

explanation.surface: A firm that predicts it will take over Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreknowledge is the faculty that sees what is coming.

clue.text: Chosen player was foremost in Brahms and Liszt

parts.note: a pick is the chosen one
led means was at the front

explanation.surface: A selected musician took the lead in a Brahms and Liszt concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brahms and Liszt' is British rhyming slang for pissed, drunk; the composers mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean intoxicated, with the slang preserved in vinegar for drunk.

clue.text: University post not new? Not new

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: A query whether a college job is fresh, answered no.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand or worn means not new.

clue.text: Doctor's agreement about new source of scurf — xerosis?

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor; the 's just joins

indicators.note: about means around, so the word goes round the letter

parts.note: yes is agreement

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A doctor agrees that the flaking on a patient is dry skin.
explanation.walkthrough: YES goes round N; the question mark flags the definition as a medical example.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerosis is the medical term for abnormal lack of moisture in skin or eyes.

clue.text: Cold water not connected in the last place you stay?

parts.note: C marks the cold water tap
off means switched off, disconnected

explanation.surface: A holiday cottage where the cold tap doesn't work.
explanation.definitionFit: A casket is where a body lies for good, so one's final resting place.

clue.text: Definite transformation in article, copper replacing iodine

indicators.note: a transformation changes the form of the word, so its letters are rearranged
replacing means one element takes the place of the other

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemistry write-up describing copper taking iodine's place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformation in' with 'replacing': ARTICLE plus CU, without I, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear and unambiguous, sharply outlined: definite.

clue.text: Work to secure old gold, without much skill

indicators.note: securing something means holding it, so the word contains the other letters

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A clumsy attempt to get hold of old gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Done badly, so with little ability: inadequately or ineptly.

clue.text: I almost stand for the flag

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to rise is to stand up

explanation.surface: Someone nearly rises in honour of the national flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is the plant, a yellow wild iris, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is the common name for wild irises growing by water.

clue.text: Peseta in former currency unexpectedly dear? I see what you're saying

indicators.note: in puts the first letter inside the following word

parts.note: the lira, plural lire, was Italy's currency before the euro
P is the abbreviation for the peseta, the old Spanish currency

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out other than planned, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paying in pesetas and lire turns out surprisingly costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads lips understands speech by watching it, as the playful definition says.

clue.text: Attempt abandoned by miserable friend

indicators.note: abandoned by means left by, so the word for an attempt is taken out

parts.note: paltry means meagre or miserable
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A mate gives up on a try, feeling wretched.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate or chum is an informal word for a friend.

clue.text: Fellow with clever story

parts.note: able means capable, clever

explanation.surface: A man with a smart tale to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: A short moral tale, often with animals, is a kind of story.

clue.text: Game incorporating situation that's a hindrance

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so one word contains the other

parts.note: deer are hunted as game
the lay of the land is its situation

explanation.surface: A sport that contains a setup which slows things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is the hunted animal, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: One who holds things up or stalls is an obstacle, a hindrance.

clue.text: Bowlers lacking power? They don't do the right things

definitions.text: They don't do the right things

indicators.note: lacking means without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: spinners are slow bowlers in cricket

explanation.surface: Cricket bowlers without strength who behave badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowlers' might be hats; they are cricket spin bowlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoers are people who transgress, failing to act rightly.
